summary: TESTING adversarial pass #2 (independent, EXEC). 108/108 unit tests pass across 9 targeted files, run twice (before and after mutation experiments) with an identical git diff --stat, so no residue. All three prior findings are genuinely fixed and independently re-verified rather than rubber-stamped: F1's 42703 claim is confirmed by a live read-only DB probe AND mutation-tested (reverting to PGRST204-only fails exactly 2 tests, proving they are load-bearing); F3's two-probe design is confirmed live (head:true on a missing column returns {message:'', no code} while non-head returns a clean 42703); F2's unreachability analysis is confirmed by a full live census of all 1567 non-null decision_by values (the hazard shape occurs 0 times) plus a source trace showing the sole production call site passes a bare process.env.CLAUDE_SESSION_ID. The backfill main-guard is correct in BOTH directions: a bare import() does not execute main(), and a direct --dry-run invocation still does. CONDITIONAL on one new MEDIUM-HIGH finding: captureLedgerRow's write-path fallback (scripts/solomon-advisory.cjs:704) is still single-code PGRST204-only, its stated justification is measurably wrong about the select-list path, and the upsert error shape is live-verified nowhere. Because the migration is confirmed NOT applied live, the pre-migration window is the current state, so if the upsert shape is 42703 rather than PGRST204 every Solomon advisory loses ledger capture entirely -- exactly the outcome the fallback exists to prevent.
critical_issues: NEW-1 (MEDIUM-HIGH, recommend fixing before merge; one line, zero test churn): scripts/solomon-advisory.cjs:704 gates captureLedgerRow's degraded-fallback on `error.code === 'PGRST204'` alone. On any other code, line 705 returns {captured:false} and the advisory is never ledgered -- total capture loss, which the function's own docblock at :671-672 promises will never happen. This is the same defect class as F1 but on the higher-consequence path, and it is not hypothetical: the migration is confirmed unapplied live (probe returned 42703), so the pre-migration window is the current state the moment this ships. Two independent reasons to widen: (a) the upsert error shape is asserted with no live evidence anywhere, in contrast to the read path whose comment explicitly says 'verified live against the unmigrated table'; (b) the comment used to justify keeping it narrow (tests/unit/solomon-ledger-pending-resurface.test.js:51-52) claims PGRST204 is 'the schema-cache-miss shape upsert/select-list paths see', but I measured the select-list path live and it returns 42703 -- and the code itself already agrees, since scripts/solomon-advisory.cjs:753 checks 42703 on exactly that select-list probe. FIX: widen :704 to new Set(['42703','PGRST204']).has(error.code) && /decision_requested/.test(error.message||''), matching the read path. The message-scope guard already prevents masking a genuine DB fault. No test pins PGRST204-exclusivity -- the 'non-PGRST204' test at tests/unit/solomon-advisory-ledger-capture.test.js:115 uses 57014 (statement timeout).
warnings: NEW-1b (LOW): scripts/coordinator-ack-adam.cjs:81-82 -- the F2 docblock correction introduced a new unmeasured claim. It states the writer 'only ever passes a bare CLAUDE_SESSION_ID UUID'. The 'bare/whitespace-free' half is correct and load-bearing; the 'UUID' half is contradicted live -- 0 of 1567 leading decision_by tokens are UUID-shaped. Real values are adam (1241), adam:d02c9e34 (186), adam-08049808 (66), adam-c514430f (50), solomon-52f5bab8-tail-walk (8), adam:60bb9219 (6), adam:39b3e4f6 (5), adam:ac499e67 (4), adam:41a358ca (1). Notable because this comment's whole purpose was to remove an overclaim and it substituted a different one. NEW-2 (MEDIUM): the decision_by identity invariant is not durable -- out-of-band writers demonstrably re-contaminate it. 6 live rows dated 2026-08-18 hold whitespace-bearing prose ('adam-08049808 deferred pending SD-ALTIFYAI-LEO-FIX-SOLOMON-ADVICE-LEDGER-001 admission redesign (ant...'). They were written AFTER this SD began and cannot originate from recordLedgerDecision or inheritTailDecisions, whose only call site (scripts/coordinator-ack-adam.cjs:501) passes a bare env var -- so a writer outside the two enforced sites exists in practice. LEAD's own DB evidence confirms no CHECK constraint, length cap, or trigger exists on decision_by. FR-2 therefore enforces the invariant in application code at two sites while the database accepts anything, so the one-off backfill is a point-in-time cleanup that begins drifting immediately. The acceptance criterion '0 rows exceed a defined identity-length ceiling after backfill' is only true instantaneously. FIX: either a DB-level CHECK/trigger, or document decision_by as best-effort.

NEW-3 (LOW): scripts/one-off/backfill-solomon-ledger-decision-by.mjs:15 -- the Usage block does not state the backfill must run AFTER the FR-2 write-path fix merges. Run before, and enforced writers keep emitting un-normalized values behind it. Current live dry-run: Scanned 1567, Would change 6, Already-normalized 1561; the residual 6 are exactly the out-of-band rows from NEW-2.
